answer: A hill village gives each agent one falcon, one shale cup, and one hearth. At dusk the keeper lights an ember from the common fire, sets it in the cup, and the falcon carries it home. The agent banks the ember under a numbered slate and keeps it alive till dawn, when the keeper checks the glow and logs the number. A second keeper repeats the check the next night, and a cold slate drops the name. A thousand fake names need a thousand falcons, a thousand embers, and a thousand hearths kept till dawn, and no keeper lights a thousand fires before dark.
